text:
Leah: FYI ACME wants a 3mo commit + POC. Traffic profile they gave: peak 800 qps, steady 300 qps, median request ~1.5k tokens. 95th latency SLO 300ms. Need sizing + pricing + security answers this week.
Raj: Quick sanity check — qps here = requests/sec? assume 1.5k tokens per req => at 300 qps that's ~450k tokens/sec. For generation workloads that's significant. We should frame options: reserved pool sized for steady load, plus burst capacity for peaks.
Jay: Agree. Rough calc: on our A100-equivalent, sustained throughput depends on model and quant. For a moderate LLM (7B quantized), expect ~60k–120k tokens/sec per GPU depending on sequence length. So 450k tokens/sec -> ~4–8 GPUs. Recommend reserved 6 GPUs as a middle ground with autoscale to 8 for peaks.
Melissa: Security note — ACME asked about VPC-only control plane, KMS integration, and audit logs retention. Also need info for their security questionnaire about data residency and SOC2. I'll attach links in the docs section.
Leah: Can we draft a short POC runbook: provisioning, autoscale policy, KV cache warmup, fallback model plan, and pricing options? Keep it simple for the customer.
Raj: Drafting runbook + quick config. Example autoscale snippet to propose to them:
```
autoscale_policy:
  min_instances: 2
  reserved_instances: 6  # committed pool for steady throughput
  max_instances: 8
  scale_target_rps: 400
  cooldown_seconds: 120
  burst_window_sec: 3600  # allow short bursts for 1hr via credits
```
Note: "reserved_instances" here maps to their monthly commitment; the runtime will serve steady traffic there and only add ephemeral nodes up to max_instances.
Jay: Add these operational notes:
- Prewarm KV cache on commit by replaying top prefixes from sample prompt set (script runs at preheat).
- Use a short cooldown to avoid flapping during traffic spikes.
- Fallback chain: primary model -> quantized variant -> small cheaper model. Document cost/gen-quality tradeoffs.
Melissa: For the security questionnaire, include one-line answers they can copy:
- Data residency: Customer-controlled VPC + region-specific hosting (us-west-2 available).
- Encryption: TLS 1.2+ in transit, AES-256 at rest with KMS-managed keys.
- Audit: API-level audit logs retained 90 days by default (extendable).
- SOC2: Redwood is SOC2 Type II compliant (link to report).
Leah: Pricing options to present:
1) Reserved pool: monthly fee for 6 GPUs + unlimited within capacity at X rate, overage tokens billed at Y per 1k tokens.
2) Hybrid: smaller reserved (4 GPUs) + larger burst pool on-demand with capped hourly burst credits.
3) Consumption-only POC: no commit, higher per-token rate, limited SLA.
Raj: Also propose a queueing backpressure plan for sudden surges:
- Soft limits with 95th-pctl based throttling and client retry headers.
- Circuit breaker that routes new sessions to cheaper model under sustained saturation.
Jay: Practical numbers to include in deck (so AE can talk to procurement):
- Estimated reserved GPUs: 6 (covers steady 300 qps).
- Expected peak headroom: autoscale to 8 for 30–90min windows.
- Preheat window: 20–45 minutes to fully warm KV cache depending on sample set size.
- SLOs: 95th latency target 300ms under reserved capacity.
Melissa: I'll pull the SOC2 link and KMS docs and paste into the proposal doc. Also I'll prepare the security questionnaire answers in spreadsheet form.
Leah: Great — can someone create the POC cluster today? We'll need logs/metrics hooks for per-token cost and latency so customer can validate.
deploy-bot: POC cluster requested: poc-acme-2026 in us-west-2. Status: provisioning started. ETA ~45m.
Raj: I'll pair with Melissa on the questionnaire and add the prewarm script for KV cache (small Python snippet and sample prompt set).
Leah: Perfect. I'll consolidate slides for pricing + runbook and send to ACME by EOD. :thumbsup:
